nodes_add.note: Endocrinologist; met Maharishi 1985, directed the movement's Ayurvedic centre at Lancaster, Massachusetts, promoted Maharishi Ayur-Veda; parted from the movement in the early 1990s

nodes_add.name: Tony Nader (Maharaja Adhiraj Rajaraam)
nodes_add.note: Physician and neuroscientist; named head of the Global Country of World Peace (2000); leads the TM organisations after Maharishi's death in 2008

nodes_update.name: Maharishi Mahesh Yogi
nodes_update.note: Born Mahesh Prasad Varma (also Srivastava), 12 January 1917 or 1918 (c. 1911 in some accounts), Jabalpur in most accounts; died Vlodrop, Netherlands, 5 February 2008; cremated at the Sangam, Allahabad, 11 February 2008. Founder of Transcendental Meditation.

nodes_update.name: Brahmananda Saraswati (Jyotirmath)
nodes_update.note: Born Rajaram Mishra near Ayodhya; birth year given as 1868, 1870 or 1871; sannyasa 1904; Shankaracharya of Jyotirmath from April 1941 until his death in 1953; called Guru Dev in the TM movement

edges_upsert.note: Installed as Shankaracharya of Jyotirmath, April 1941

Disciple and secretary about thirteen years, by most accounts 1941-1953, as Bal Brahmachari Mahesh; not eligible to succeed (not a Brahmin, not a sannyasi). TM initiation ceremony honours Brahmananda as Guru Dev.
Worked and travelled with Maharishi from the mid-1970s until about 1980-81
Met Maharishi 1985; directed the movement's Ayurvedic centre at Lancaster, Massachusetts; parted in the early 1990s after the 1991 JAMA controversy (Warrier)
Named head of the Global Country of World Peace (2000) as Maharaja Adhiraj Rajaraam; took over leadership on Maharishi's death, 2008

glossary.def: A sacred sound, syllable or phrase repeated aloud or silently. In Transcendental Meditation a short Sanskrit sound is given by the teacher and thought silently, with its meaning playing no part in the practice.
A ritual of worship or honour with offerings such as flowers, fruit, light and water. In TM a short puja to the line of masters ending with Brahmananda Saraswati precedes the giving of the mantra.
An extraordinary power said to come from advanced yoga practice; Patanjali's Yoga Sutras list many. The TM-Sidhi programme, spelled that way by the movement, is Maharishi's course built on them.
A seed mantra: a one-syllable sound such as aim or shrim used in Tantric and devotional practice, traditionally associated with a particular deity.
A celibate student devoted to a teacher or to sacred study; a stage before, or apart from, full monastic renunciation.

maharishi: Born Mahesh Prasad Varma, 12 Jan 1917 (disputed; 1911/1918 also given), Jabalpur; Kayastha; father Ram Prasad; secretary to Brahmananda 1941 as Bal Brahmachari Mahesh; physics degree Allahabad 1942; could not succeed (not Brahmin); Uttarkashi 1953; 1955 Kerala, Transcendental Deep Meditation, Beacon Light of the Himalayas; 1957 Madras seminar, Spiritual Regeneration Movement; 1958-59 world tour; 1961 first TTC Rishikesh ~60; 1963 Science of Being; 1966 SIMS; 1968 Seelisberg; 1970 Maine/California courses; 1973 MIU classes Santa Barbara; 1974 Fairfield; 1975 Age of Enlightenment; TM-Sidhi 1975/76; 1988 Indian tax dispute; 1990 Vlodrop; 1991 illness per Chopra; 1992 NLP; 2000 GCWP with Nader; 2002 Larry King; Times quote on money; theory of mantras quote -> https://en-academic.com/dic.nsf/enwiki/118951

Physics degree Allahabad 1942; IMS 1959; SIMS 1966; Chopra parted ~1994; Time/Newsweek reported Indian scholars' criticism as oversimplified -> https://www.ebsco.com/research-starters/health-and-medicine/maharishi-mahesh-yogi

Died 5 Feb 2008 about 7 p.m., Vlodrop, per Bob Roth, natural causes; born reportedly 12 Jan 1917; refused to discuss early life; secretary to holy man; two-year retreat; taught from 1955, US 1959; moved to monastery grounds Vlodrop 1990; quote 'the unified field of all the laws of nature' -> https://www.hinduismtoday.com/hpi/?p=6579
Lay in state at Allahabad ashram; cremated Monday at Sangam; ~2,000 foreign followers and ~5,000 Indians; Maharaja Adhiraj Rajaraam took over -> https://www.nbcnews.com/id/wbna23096121
Retirement into silence Jan 2008, quote 'I think I have done whatever can be done'; Rajaraam heads GCWP; Hagelin NLP 2000; mantra 'meaningless' per Roth -> https://religionnews.com/?p=29024
Spokesman: personal fortune 'may exceed $1 billion'; Gilpin $2-3 billion; fees ~$35 late 1960s to $2,500 -> https://www.npr.org/transcripts/87890203

Hilton lecture 24 Aug 1967, attendees, Ringo absent (son born 19 Aug), 90-minute audience, Euston train 25 Aug with Jagger and Faithfull, Cynthia held back by security guard, Epstein found dead 27 Aug; quote 'such practical and intelligent young boys' -> https://beatlesbible.com/people/maharishi-mahesh-yogi
